facts: **$A = \tfrac{1}{2}r^{2}\theta$**, where $r$ is the radius and $\theta$ is the central angle **in radians**.
If the angle is in degrees, convert it first using $\theta = \text{degrees} \times \dfrac{\pi}{180^{\circ}}$.
Since $l = r\theta$, the area can also be written as $A = \tfrac{1}{2}rl$.
Rearranging gives the radius $r = \sqrt{\dfrac{2A}{\theta}}$ and the angle $\theta = \dfrac{2A}{r^{2}}$.
A **minor sector** has $\theta < \pi$ and a **major sector** has $\theta > \pi$, where $\theta_{\text{major}} = 2\pi - \theta_{\text{minor}}$.
steps: Ensure the central angle $\theta$ is in radians (convert from degrees if needed).
Substitute the known values (or rearrange to solve for $r$ or $\theta$).
Evaluate and state the exact area with $\pi$ or round to the specified accuracy.

workedExamples.question_text: A sector has radius $7\text{ cm}$ and central angle $1.2$ radians. Find its area.
A sprinkler waters a sector of radius $10\text{ m}$ through an angle of $75^{\circ}$. Find the exact watered area.
A sector has radius $8\text{ cm}$ and arc length $6\pi\text{ cm}$. Find its exact area.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Find the central angle using $l=r\theta$.

$\begin{align*}6\pi &= 8\theta\\\theta &= \frac{3\pi}{4}\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}A &= \tfrac12r^2\theta\\A &= \tfrac12\times8^2\times\frac{3\pi}{4}\\A &= 24\pi\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: A sector has area $18\pi\text{ cm}^2$ and central angle $\frac{\pi}{4}$ radians. Find its exact radius.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}A &= \tfrac12r^2\theta\\18\pi &= \tfrac12r^2\times\frac{\pi}{4}\\r^2 &= 144\\r &= 12\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

Take the positive square root because a radius is positive.

workedExamples.question_text: A sector of radius $10\text{ cm}$ has area $\frac{25\pi}{3}\text{ cm}^2$. Find its central angle in radians and degrees.

workedExamples.solution_text:
Use the angle of the remaining region.

$\begin{align*}\theta_{\text{major}} &= 360^{\circ}-90^{\circ}\\\theta_{\text{major}} &= 270^{\circ}\\\theta_{\text{major}} &= \frac{3\pi}{2}\text{ radians}\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}A &= \tfrac12r^2\theta_{\text{major}}\\A &= \tfrac12\times8^2\times\frac{3\pi}{2}\\A &= 48\pi\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$

$\theta=120^{\circ}\times\frac{\pi}{180^{\circ}}=\frac{2\pi}{3}$.

Subtract the inner sector from the outer sector.

$\begin{align*}A_{\text{outer}} &= \tfrac12\times24^2\times\frac{2\pi}{3}\\A_{\text{outer}} &= 192\pi\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}A_{\text{inner}} &= \tfrac12\times12^2\times\frac{2\pi}{3}\\A_{\text{inner}} &= 48\pi\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}A_{\text{swept}} &= 192\pi-48\pi\\A_{\text{swept}} &= 144\pi\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$

mastery.question_text:
A decorative folding fan is constructed with fabric mounted between two concentric circular arcs of radii $16\text{ cm}$ and $24\text{ cm}$.
When fully opened, the fan subtends a central angle of $\theta = \dfrac{5\pi}{8}\text{ radians}$.
Find the exact area of the fabric covering the region between the two arcs.
mastery.solution_text:
The area of the fabric is the difference between the areas of the outer and inner sectors:
$A_{\text{outer}} = \tfrac{1}{2}R^{2}\theta = \tfrac{1}{2} \times 24^{2} \times \dfrac{5\pi}{8} = 180\pi\text{ cm}^{2}$
$A_{\text{inner}} = \tfrac{1}{2}r^{2}\theta = \tfrac{1}{2} \times 16^{2} \times \dfrac{5\pi}{8} = 80\pi\text{ cm}^{2}$
$\text{Fabric area} = A_{\text{outer}} - A_{\text{inner}}$
$= 180\pi - 80\pi$
$= 100\pi\text{ cm}^{2}$
